text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime minister Andris Shkele has warned the co-operation council of governing parties that he will resign unless the parliamentary committee investigating the distribution of the G-24 loans stops spreading allegations that he was involved in their distribution.
- Italian president Oscar Luigi Scalfaro, who is on an official visit in Latvia, had talks with President Guntis Ulmanis. They discussed Italy's support for Latvia's bids for NATO and EU membership.
- Alexei Vidavski, the mayor of Daugavpils, sent a letter to President Ulmanis complaining about the depiction of his city in the Latvian press and requesting a meeting with the president.
- Parliament rejected the idea of forced privatisation of apartments, suggested by the minister of economics.
- The Baltic transit conference opened yesterday in Riga. It is attended by 250 representatives from 15 countries.

- The state auditor admits most foreign loans taken by Latvia have been misused and is skeptical about the possibility of paying them back. On January 1, 1997, Latvia's foreign debt amounted to 240 million lats, of which only 227 lats have been guaranteed by the government.
- Last year the company Latvijas Finieris (Latvian Plywood) had a profit of 4.253 million lats on turnover of 33.7 million lats.
- Food producers from Daugavpils and nearby districts will exhibit their production at the international fair Mosprodyarmarka on June 11-12 in Moscow.
